_readme: THE BOX ITSELF — which tenants this bench has, which stores live in each, and the instance settings every
screen inherits. Applied by `bin/seed-box.mjs`, ONE TENANT PER RUN (the write face takes the tenant as a
header, so a run is scoped to one by construction).
★ WHY THIS FILE EXISTS INSTEAD OF `stores` IN `catalog.json`. That list has NO TENANT AXIS — it is a flat
array from the days this bench had one tenant, and it cannot say which of two tenants a store belongs to.
The topology it could not express is now the point: two brands, four stores, one admin container. So the
TERRAIN (tenants, stores, settings) is declared here and the CATALOGUE stays over there.
⚠️ `catalog.json` STILL CARRIES A `stores` ARRAY and it is now SUPERSEDED. It is not deleted here because
that file is being restructured by another slice in this same wave, and two hands in one file is how a
merge eats a decision. Until it goes, `bin/seed.mjs` may still create a store from it — which is
IDEMPOTENT (it skips a handle that exists) but would put it in whichever tenant that run is pointed at.
Point that script at the right tenant, or let this one run first.
★ `require_shipping_document` LIVES HERE FOR A REASON WORTH READING. It is what makes the shipping
widget grow its fiscal block, and it used to be switched on at the end of a LOGISTICS function inside the
history executor. It is tenant configuration, like the three settings beside it, and tenant configuration
written by a data seeder is the thing that surprises somebody in three months looking for where it was
turned on. Same reason the currency is declared even though it is already the default: the place a switch
is declared should be the place a reader would look for it.
⇒ THE TWO TENANTS DISAGREE ABOUT IT ON PURPOSE — `forgeco` requires the document, `forgecafe` does not —
and both say so in words. See `_settings_why` on the coffee tenant for what the OFF side changes and what
was measured.
★★ `dataset` — WHOSE CATALOGUE THE MOUNTED EXAMPLE DATA IS, AND IT IS THE FIELD THIS FILE EXISTS
TO CARRY. A box mounts ONE example dataset (`FORGE_SEED_DATASET_DIR`), and a dataset is a BRAND's: this
one is the footwear catalogue. `dist/seed-demo.js` fills the tenant it is POINTED AT — correctly, from
whatever dataset is mounted — so pointing it at a second tenant fills a coffee shop with shoes. Measured
on the bench of 02/09: `forgecafe` held 2 811 products (21 curated + the dataset's 2 790), 44 490 SKUs,
351 footwear brands and the dataset's eleven footwear custom fields. The kernel did nothing wrong — the
same handles carry DIFFERENT ids in the two schemas, so those were two correctly-scoped writes, not a
leak. The defect was `bin/box-up.sh` running step 9 `for t in $TENANTS`. This field is what it reads now.
★ AND THE TENANT THAT DOES NOT CARRY IT NEEDS THE OTHER HALF OF THAT ONE-SHOT. `seed-demo.js` fuses two
jobs: fill the store from the dataset, and PROVISION the tenant (its apps, its delivery, its checkout
flags). Only the first is the dataset's. So a `dataset: false` tenant declares `apps` and `delivery`
here, `bin/seed-box.mjs` applies them at step 6, and the tenant stands without borrowing another brand's
catalogue. ⚠️ A `dataset: true` tenant must NOT declare them — the one-shot is their owner, and two
owners for one gesture is how this repository has already grown a duplicate.
★★★ `domain` / `admin_domain` — THE ADDRESS EACH FACE OF THIS BOX IS PUBLISHED AT (pk34/d1). The demo
publishes SIX addresses, and FOUR of them had nowhere to be
declared: `FORGE_DOMAIN`, `FORGE_ADMIN_DOMAIN` and `FORGE_TOTEM_DOMAIN` are three SINGULAR variables for
a box with two brands, four stores and two admins, so the outlet and the coffee shop had no variable at
all and the second admin was a file somebody hand-wrote into `caddy/extra/`.
★ A HOSTNAME IS DATA AND BELONGS HERE; WHICH CONTAINER SERVES IT IS THE EDGE'S. A store's public
hostname is the `host` column the kernel keys its directory on (`storePublicUrl`/`storeHostKey`) and an
admin's is what `read.admin.by_host` resolves — both are facts about the TOPOLOGY, which is what this
file states. `caddy/Caddyfile` turns a hostname into an upstream and nothing here names a container. The
wire between the two is `env`, because Caddy cannot read this file: `bin/box-domains.guard.mjs` grades
the pairing in BOTH directions, plus the third end nobody had — compose has to DELIVER that variable to
the edge container.
⚠️ THE BENCH NAMES NONE OF THEM AND NOTHING CHANGES. The box is born on `localhost` (§0b) and the
promotion is a NAMED step; `.env.example` leaves every one of these variables empty, the bench opts into
`caddy/Caddyfile.local`, and these lines are inert there. A DEPLOYMENT sets the six.
⚠️ `directory: false` IS THE EXCEPTION AND IT DECLARES ITSELF, exactly as `status` and `gate` do: the
hostname is the EDGE's (a front of this box answers there) and the KERNEL's address book must NOT claim
it for that store. Today there is exactly one — the counter — and the measurement is in its
`_public_url_why` below.
WHAT IS NOT HERE, and deliberately: the FIRST store of each tenant. `provision-ref` creates it at
bootstrap (`FORGE_REF_STORE_HANDLE`), before any credential exists to drive the port with — so listing it
here would be a second author for a row that already has one. It is named below only so a reader can see
the whole shape, with `bootstrap: true` marking who really makes it.

_why: ★★ A BIRTH IS NOT DONE WHEN THE BOX IS UP — IT IS DONE WHEN THE BOX IS WARM, and the argument is
commercial rather than tidy: this box is evaluated on performance too, and failing a performance test
costs a sale. A box handed over cold makes
the first visitor — who may be the person evaluating it — pay for every cache this box could have filled
by itself. So `bin/warm-box.mjs` runs at the end of every birth.
★★ BUT IT REPORTS AND DOES NOT GRADE — this step is a REPORT by decision. Measured on three
real births: the warmer plans ~420 pages plus ~20 400 IMAGE derivatives found in each page's `srcset`,
against the VITRINE's own 15-minute DEFAULT — so EVERY run ended `15865 urls were never visited`, and the
step was red on every birth by construction. It also invented red: `failed=198` during a birth against
`failed=0` for the same urls on the idle box minutes later, because it is the last step of the birth and
races the tail of the seed. ★ A step that is ALWAYS red is a step people learn to skip, and then it is
worth nothing on the day it is right. So `bin/box-up.sh` prints
what the run learned — every url that did not answer BY NAME, and every one that was never VISITED, which
is a different thing — and does not fail the birth on it. ⛔ What it DOES still fail on is a store this
file DECLARES and the box does not hold: that is not warmth, it is a birth that did not build something.
★★ pk21 — AND THE FIRST OF THOSE TWO IS GONE: THE RUN'S CEILING DERIVES FROM THE PLAN, never from a
constant. It was never true that this box could not raise the vitrine's default — the prose
here said so and was WRONG: `/api/warm?max_duration_ms=` overrides it (the product's own warm route). A
run that is CUT is now re-run under a ceiling of (urls PLANNED + the urls the verify pass revisits) ×
(the ms-per-url that run MEASURED), both taken from the run itself. Nothing about that number lives in
this file, and deliberately so: a constant here would fit today's catalogue and lie again the day it
grows. What is NOT repaired is the false red — that one is still just a report.
WHICH STORES: every store the PORT reports for the tenant, minus the ones the PORT itself says have no
public page (`storefront_enabled: false`, derived from the store's `status`) — and a skip is ANNOUNCED by
name, with that reason. ★ pk21: THIS FILE NO LONGER DECLARES SERVABILITY. It used to mark the counter
`servable: false` by hand, which was a second truth about a store the same read already answered, with
nothing to keep the two in agreement; the derivation lives in `bin/servable.mjs` and both steps read it.
The list is the box's, never this field's: a store created tomorrow is classified with no edit here, and a
store this file does not mention is warmed and NAMED as undeclared.
⚠️ `threshold_ms` IS NULL AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. A latency ceiling nobody measured is an invented
promise, and a run that fails a number nobody chose is exactly the prose-that-lies this repository keeps
paying for (the product's own `WarmOptions.thresholdMs` says the same in the same words). Null ⇒ the run
asserts that every page WARMED, and says out loud that it asserts nothing about how fast. Put a number
here — measured on this box — and every birth from then on grades it.

online_only.what: Purge the CDN in front of this box, so it stops serving the DEAD box's pages.
online_only.order_why: ⚠️ AFTER THE REBIRTH, NEVER BEFORE, and the order is the whole point: a CDN purged first refills itself with the old origin's answers during the ~17 minutes the birth takes, and comes out of the reset holding exactly what the purge was for. The sequence is reborn → purge → warm → verdict.
online_only.bench_why: There is no CDN in front of the bench: `caddy` is the edge and it caches nothing. So on this box the driver resolves to `none` and the step is a no-op that SAYS SO — a silent step here would read as work done.

online_only.what: Drop the object prefix the PREVIOUS birth wrote, which nothing points at any more.
online_only.order_why: After the rebirth for the same reason as the edge: the keys to keep are the ones the new birth just wrote, and they do not exist until it has.
online_only.bench_why: On the bench the media is a docker VOLUME and `bin/box-down.sh` destroys it by name, so the previous birth's bytes are already gone before this step could run. ONLINE it is a bucket, and a bucket is not a volume: the rebirth uploads a fresh set of keys and last week's stay, paid for and pointed at by nothing. Nothing breaks — it only grows.

tenants.why: T1, the footwear brand. The tenant this bench was born with, kept under its own name so nothing that already refers to it has to move.

admin_domain._why: The address a DEPLOYMENT publishes this tenant's admin at, beside the bench's own door above. Two lines for one face because they answer two different questions: `admin_host` is what a browser types on THIS laptop and what `platform.admin_host.set` claims in the directory at birth; this is what the edge is told to serve and certify online. The promotion is what makes the second become the first.

tenants._dataset_why: The mounted example data IS this brand's catalogue — 2 790 footwear products, 351 footwear brands, and the footwear facet vocabulary in its `custom-fields.json`. So step 9 of `bin/box-up.sh` runs here, and everything it brings (the catalogue, the storefront apps, the delivery methods, the checkout flags) has one owner: the one-shot.

stores.name: Forge

domain._why: The demo's root shop, on the reference vitrine plus the checkout we host — ONE hostname split by PATH, never two. A subdomain for the checkout would put `forge_cart` and `forge_customer_session` on another origin and the shopper would lose the cart on the way to paying, which is why every shop face of this box carries the same doors and `bin/box-domains.guard.mjs` compares them against each other.

stores.why: The reference storefront, unforked and unthemed. It is the control: every other store's thesis is that a theme plus data plus composition is enough, and a thesis needs something to be compared against.

stores.name: Forge Outlet

domain._why: ★ THE SECOND SHOP ON THE SAME CONTAINERS, and until pk34 it had no address at all: `FORGE_DOMAIN` is singular, so this store could only ever be reached through the bench's `/s/<id>` path space. It runs the reference vitrine UNFORKED — the whole thesis of this store is that a theme plus data is enough — so its hostname reaches the same two containers the root shop does, and the only thing that makes it the outlet is which store the kernel's directory says answers here.

stores._checkout_posture_why: ★★ A22 — POSTURE 2 OF 3: NO GUEST, BUT A RECOGNISED BUYER IS SPARED THE TYPING. An outlet lives on returning bargain hunters, so it asks for an identity and then asks for as little as possible. Measured before this line existed (04/09): guest=t (the column's default) and masked=f, i.e. this store had no posture at all — it had the accident of two defaults. ⚠️ THE SIBLING `forge` DELIBERATELY DECLARES NOTHING: step 9 (`dist/seed-demo.js` → `configureStore`) re-asserts masked+guest ON for the tenant's BOOTSTRAP store on every run, AFTER this script, so a declaration there would be overwritten in silence — `bootstrapFlagConflicts` in seed/posture.mjs refuses it by name. Its posture (permit both) is therefore the one-shot's and happens to be exactly the one the contrast wants.
stores.why: The same catalogue under a theme of its own. Second store of T1, created through the port.

tenants.why: T2, the coffee business. A SECOND TENANT, which this bench never had — and the thing that makes it possible is not a second admin container: `read.admin.by_host` resolves the tenant from the request's host:port and `platform.admin_host.set` writes that map, so one admin serves both.

admin_domain._why: ★★ THE SECOND ADMIN, AND UNTIL pk34 IT WAS THE ONE FACE OF THIS BOX THAT COULD ONLY BE HAND-WRITTEN. `FORGE_ADMIN_DOMAIN` is singular and this box has two brands, so the coffee tenant's admin had to be a file somebody dropped into `caddy/extra/` per box — the recipe is still in that folder's README and it is still right for a THIRD tenant, but a face every deployment of this instance has is not an extra. Same container as the first (`read.admin.by_host` resolves the tenant from the Host), different hostname, different session cookie.

tenants._dataset_why: A coffee business is not the brand the mounted example data describes. Its catalogue is the CURATED one this repository writes — 6 coffees + the counter's 15 — and nothing else belongs in it. Step 9 therefore does not run here; `apps` and `delivery` below are the half of that one-shot this tenant really did need.
_apps_why: THE APPS STEP 9 USED TO INSTALL HERE AS A SIDE EFFECT OF FILLING A CATALOGUE THIS TENANT SHOULD NEVER
HAVE HAD. Measured on the bench of 02/09 (`forge_control.extension_installation`): six landed in
`forgecafe` at 00:59:41, inside `seedCuratedStorefront` — the second half of the dataset one-shot.
`reviews` and `subscriptions` are NOT here and must not be: `seed/coffee.mjs` installs those, and one
gesture may only have one owner.
⚠️ `payment-reference` is why a coffee cart can be paid at all — a store with no payment app reaches
the payment step with no method, which is a dead end that reads as a broken checkout.
`admin-dashboard` is what puts the widgets on this tenant's admin home — seven of them, not the
three this line claimed until 10/09. ★ AND IT DOES NOT DECIDE THEIR ORDER: an install auto-places
each widget at the END of the slot, so the order an install leaves is the order the apps were
installed in. What decides it is the mounted dataset's `admin_widgets`, applied to EVERY tenant by
`seed/widgets.mjs` in the window phase and graded per tenant by `bin/verify-seed.mjs`. Before that
existed this tenant's board was right by accident and `forgeco`'s was wrong, from the same rule.
★★ A14 — `payment-mercadopago` LEFT THIS LIST, AND THE LINE IT TAKES WITH IT IS THE POINT.
It does not need to arrive installed: it is an interesting feature that has to be EXPLAINED, so it
belongs to a demo somebody gives on purpose, installed by hand at that moment. So the app stays
COMPOSED — it is still in `composition.json`, still in the image, still a row in the admin's Apps
area anyone can install with two clicks — and simply is not installed at birth.
⚠️ THE VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE, NAMED SO NOBODY FILES IT AS A BUG: the checkout's «Pagar com» line
DISAPPEARS. It is not a regression, it is the mechanism working: with one provider per method
`candidates.length > 1` is false and the second line does not render, with the reason written in the
source — «a store with one provider per method has no choice to offer, and offering one would be
inventing a decision» (`PaymentStep.tsx:477`). Wanting the choice visible again is a SECOND
SIMULATOR, never the Mercado Pago.
⛔ `payment-pos` IS NOT ON THIS LIST AND MUST NOT JOIN IT — `seed/coffee.mjs` owns it, and it is what
the counter's totem charges through. `payment-zero` is not here either, and adding it would be
INVENTING a capability this tenant never had rather than removing one that was asked for.
_delivery_why: A COFFEE SHOP THAT DELIVERS NEEDS ITS OWN FREIGHT, and until now it borrowed the footwear seeder's. Same
two methods and the same figures `demo-data`'s `populate` writes — deliberately, so nothing a human has
already tested changes shape — but declared HERE, by the box, for the tenant that owns them.
⛔ IT IS ALSO A PRECONDITION OF STEP 10, NOT A GARNISH. `seed-history` refuses a tenant with more than one
active delivery method, and box-up silences all but the one named by $FORGE_HISTORY_KEEP_METHOD
("Entrega Padrão") — a tenant with NO delivery method fails that step by name. So this is applied at
step 6, before the curated seed, the past and the window: exactly where `bin/seed-box.mjs` runs.
⚠️ TENANT-WIDE, no `store_id` — the same limitation `seed/totem.json` writes up for the counter's pickup:
these commands have no store axis, so the counter's checkout sees these two as well.
_settings_why: ★ `require_shipping_document` IS DECLARED `false` HERE, AND THE WORD `false` IS THE POINT — the key is
not simply dropped. The kernel's own default is already `false` (tenant/0086_shipment_lifecycle.sql),
so a newborn box would land on the same value with no line at all; a box that is RE-SEEDED rather than
reborn would not, because `bin/seed-box.mjs` sends exactly the keys this object carries and an absent
one leaves the column as it was found. Declaring the OFF state is also the rule the `_readme` above
states for the currency: the place a switch is declared should be the place a reader would look for it,
and a gate that is off by silence is a gate nobody can find.
⚠️ WHAT IT CHANGES, MEASURED ON THE BENCH 2026-09-15. The gate is the only input of `awaiting_document`
in `deriveShipmentStage` (packages/core/src/order/shipment-stage.ts): with it off, a parcel in the queue
with no document attached is `preparing` instead, so the expedition widget's document bar reads zero
for this tenant. 86 parcels of this tenant sat in that bar — 68 of `cafe`, 18 of `balcao` — and they
are back in the ordinary queue.
★ AND THE CAPABILITY IS STILL DEMONSTRATED BY THE BOX: `forgeco` keeps the gate ON, with 101 parcels
(75 of `forge`, 26 of `outlet`) in that same bar. One brand requires the paperwork and the other does
not, which is a better demonstration of a per-instance switch than two brands agreeing by accident.
⛔ NOTHING IN THE SEED DEPENDS ON IT BEING ON. The history executor attaches a document only when the
plan says the parcel carries one and only ships parcels that do (`apps/api/src/seed-history.ts`), and
the gate can only ever REFUSE `order.shipment.mark_shipped` — turning it off relaxes and requires
nothing, so no step of this box can fail because of this line.
📌 IT IS A TENANT SETTING AND THIS TENANT HAS TWO STORES. `instance_settings` has no store axis, so the
e-commerce and the counter cannot disagree about it. That is a known limitation of the kernel and not
something this file may work around.

stores.name: Forge Café

domain._why: ★★ THE FORK'S OWN HOSTNAME — the one face of this box whose vitrine is not ours. `storefront-coffee` is a deployable of this repository, so this hostname's fall-through is that container while its `/checkout*`, `/account*` and the rest stay with the checkout we host: the customisation posture this demo exists to show, at an address. ⚠️ AND IT NEEDS ONE DOOR ITS SIBLINGS DO NOT: the fork carries `assetPrefix: '/_coffee'` in its image (storefront-coffee/next.config.mjs), unconditionally, so it emits `/_coffee/_next/…` into its HTML on EVERY hostname and answers 404 to it — the edge has to strip that prefix here or the coffee shop is served UNSTYLED with nothing in any log. `caddy/Caddyfile` carries it beside the shared import.

stores._gate_why: ⛔⛔ THE `gate` FIELD IS GONE FROM THIS FILE AND FROM EVERYTHING THAT READ IT (v0.4), AND THE ABSENCE IS THE DECISION. It used to let ONE store opt out of the demo's front door, with the reason written beside it. There is no front door to opt out of: the app that filled `storefront:gate` left this repository, because the cost of that slot is not the screen but the ROUTING — the product asks at the edge of EVERY store route whether an INSTALLED app fills it, so one install answered `private, no-cache, no-store` on every route of every store and handed a robot an interstitial with no `<title>` at every url (measured on the deployed box, 18/09). A per-store `gate: false` could never have bought the cacheable tree back for the others. ★ THE SENTENCE A VISITOR IS OWED IS A BLOCK NOW — `demo-setup/demo_ribbon`, placed in Compose, per store — and `bin/prove-doors.mjs` grades the OPPOSITE rule: no door of this box may serve a gate. ⚠️ THE REASON IS KEPT RATHER THAN DELETED because a reader who finds no line at all cannot tell a decision from an oversight.
stores._checkout_posture_why: ★★ A22 — POSTURE 3 OF 3: NEITHER. A coffee shop that sells subscriptions and a loyalty relationship wants an account, not an anonymous sale, so it asks the buyer to sign in and recognises nobody who has not. This REPLACES the `masked_checkout_enabled: true` this store carried since 02/09, and the replacement is the point of the whole item: the demo's three shops used to answer this question identically by accident, which demonstrates nothing. ⚠️ DECLARING IT HERE IS LEGAL AND ON `forge` IT WOULD NOT BE — this tenant is `dataset: false`, so no step 9 runs against it and nobody else writes these columns.
stores.why: The coffee e-commerce, on its forked storefront. Born in T2 rather than moved into it: data does not travel sideways between tenants, so on a virgin box this is simply where it is created.

stores.name: Forge Café · Balcão

domain._why: The counter's front is the TOTEM — one app of this repository's own serving every path of this host, no second Next server behind it, no store in the URL and nothing to split. So this face has a hostname like every other and `directory: false` beside it, which is the whole distinction pk34 had to draw: WHERE A FRONT OF THIS BOX ANSWERS is not the same fact as WHAT THE KERNEL'S ADDRESS BOOK CLAIMS FOR THAT STORE. The edge serves this name; the store's `host` column stays null. `_public_url_why` below is the measurement that keeps it null, and `bin/prove-doors.mjs` asserts the negative — a store declared `directory: false` whose hostname the directory HAS claimed is red by name.

stores._checkout_posture_why: ⛔ THE COUNTER DECLARES NO POSTURE, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY — A22's table reads «Café / Balcão: neither», and applying it here would BREAK THE TOTEM. `totem/src/lib/buyer.ts:70` sends `guest: true` on every counter order (a person at a kiosk typed a name, not an address), and `checkout.place_order` refuses a pure-guest cart with `forbidden · guest_disabled` when the store's flag is off (packages/core/src/commands/checkout.ts:787). So `guest_checkout_enabled: false` here is a counter that cannot sell coffee. The contrast A22 is built on is between the THREE SERVABLE SHOPS — Forge, Outlet, Café — and this fourth store is the totem's, not a shop a browser reaches. `masked_checkout_enabled` is already `false` here (the column's default) and is left unstated for the same reason it always was: a totem has no returning session to recognise.
stores._servability_why: ★★ THE COUNTER IS OFF THE STREET, AND THE `status` ABOVE IS THE WHOLE OF IT (pk22). The merchant of this shop chose another front — the totem IS the counter's front — so the reference vitrine must not serve it, and `private` is the kernel's word for exactly that. ⛔ IT IS WRITTEN THROUGH THE PORT AND NOWHERE ELSE: `bin/seed-box.mjs` carries it on `tenant.store.create` and converges it with `tenant.store.update` (pk13/C6 put it on the create so the store is never public for the window between the two). No SQL, no column touched behind the port. ★ AND EVERYTHING ELSE FOLLOWS BY ITSELF, WITH NO LIST ANYWHERE: `read.internal.stores` derives `storefront_enabled: false` from this word (`storefrontIsEnabled` — `status !== 'private'`, packages/core/src/commands/store.ts), `bin/servable.mjs` reads that, and steps 14 (warm) and 14-bis (doors) skip the counter's PAGE by name with the port's own reason. ⚠️ `private` IS NOT `archived`, AND THE COUNTER IS THE PROOF. Measured by pk21/p1 with the store private: `read.products`, `product.by_handle`, `search`, `categories`, `availability`, `store.by_host`, `cart` and `checkout` all answer 200, and `cart.create` + `add_line` still work. So the totem keeps selling, `/s/<balcao>/checkout` and `/s/<balcao>/account/login` keep answering — they are the CHECKOUT deployable, which mounts `requireStore` and never `requirePublicStorefront` — and the admin keeps showing everything. One thing stops: the vitrine's page. ★ THIS IS NOT THE `servable: false` THIS STORE CARRIED UNTIL pk21 COMING BACK, and the difference is the whole of pk21+pk22: that flag was a SECOND TRUTH about a fact the port already published, with nothing to keep the two in agreement. This is the kernel's own column, and servability is what DERIVES from it. Put the counter back on the street with `"status": "active"` here (or by dropping the key — an undeclared status is «this box has no opinion» and the column keeps what it has), never by editing `bin/servable.mjs`, `bin/warm-box.mjs` or `bin/prove-doors.mjs`.
stores._public_url_why: ⛔ THE COUNTER DECLARES NO PUBLIC URL, AND IT WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS REFUSED (pk22). pk21/p1 made the vitrine REDIRECT (307) a store with no public page to the address that store declares, instead of 404ing it — so declaring the TOTEM's address here would make `/s/<balcao>` hand the visitor to the counter's real front, which is the exact capability this demo exists to show. Three measurements said no. (1) ⚠️ `public_url` IS THE `host` COLUMN (`storePublicUrl`/`storeHostKey`, packages/core/src/read/host-key.ts) AND THE KERNEL ALSO WRITES IT INTO TRANSACTIONAL MESSAGES: `packages/core/src/notification/context.ts:176` builds `https://<host>` and `order.url = <that>/account/orders/<id>`, and the factory templates draw the «Acompanhar o pedido» button only `{{#if order.url}}` (factory-content/variants.ts:70). The totem serves ONE route (`totem/src/app/page.tsx`) and no `/account/*`, so every counter receipt would grow a button leading to the totem's own 404 — over `https`, at a plain-HTTP port, on this bench. Today `host` is null, the button is absent, and nothing is broken. (2) ⚠️ THIS REASON WAS REWRITTEN BY pk34 AND ITS OLD FORM IS GONE, because the slice that named the demo's six addresses made it false. It used to say «the address is the BOX's and not the dataset's, while this file is applied identically on every box» — and this file now DOES carry the counter's address, in `domain` above. What it says instead is the distinction that survived: declaring WHERE A FRONT OF THIS BOX IS PUBLISHED is not claiming that hostname in the KERNEL'S ADDRESS BOOK for this store. `domain.directory` is false here for exactly that, and it is the only face of this box where the two answers differ. (3) ⛔ AND THIS REASON IS SIMPLY DEAD — MEASURED 2026-09-12 AND IT NO LONGER HOLDS. It used to say the images this box pins predate pk21/p1 (`forge.lock` from `v03/integra@8f302fbe7`) and publish no `public_url` at all.
